skill_title: Find the resultant of perpendicular vectors and resolve a vector into components

items.question: What is the resultant of two vectors?
items.expectedAnswer: The single vector that has the same effect as the vectors combined.
items.explanation: The resultant is one vector equivalent in effect to all the vectors added together.
options: The single vector that has the same effect as the vectors combined.
The average of the two vectors.

items.question: Which method finds the magnitude of the resultant of two PERPENDICULAR vectors?
items.explanation: Perpendicular vectors form a right angle, so the resultant magnitude uses Pythagoras.

items.question: A force of 3 N east and 4 N north act on a point. What is the magnitude of the resultant?
A vector of magnitude 10 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. What is its horizontal component? (cos30° = 0.866)
items.explanation: Horizontal component = Fcosθ = 10 × cos30° = 8.66 N.

items.question: A vector of magnitude 10 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. What is its vertical component? (sin30° = 0.5)
items.explanation: Vertical component = Fsinθ = 10 × sin30° = 5 N.

items.question: Why must the direction of a resultant always be stated?
items.expectedAnswer: Because a resultant is a vector, which needs magnitude and direction.
items.explanation: A resultant is a vector; without a direction it is incomplete.
options: Because the magnitude is always unknown.
Because a resultant is a vector, which needs magnitude and direction.

items.question: Two perpendicular forces, 6 N and 8 N, act on a body. What is the magnitude of the resultant?
When you resolve a single vector into perpendicular components, the components are...
items.expectedAnswer: always smaller than the original vector.
items.explanation: Components are projections, so each is smaller than (or equal to) the original vector.
options: always larger than the original vector.
always smaller than the original vector.
equal to the original vector each.

items.question: Two perpendicular displacements, 5 m and 12 m, are added. What is the magnitude of the resultant displacement?
A velocity vector points due east. What is its component in the north direction?
items.explanation: A vector along east has no north component (the perpendicular component is zero).

items.question: Two perpendicular forces of 9 N and 12 N act on an object. Find the magnitude of the resultant.
A resultant force of 5 N acts east and 5 N acts north on an object. What angle does the resultant make with the east direction?
items.explanation: tanθ = opposite/adjacent = 5/5 = 1, so θ = 45°.

items.question: A box is pulled with a 20 N force at 60° to the horizontal. What is the horizontal component? (cos60° = 0.5)
items.explanation: Horizontal = Fcosθ = 20 × cos60° = 20 × 0.5 = 10 N.

items.question: A box is pulled with a 20 N force at 60° to the horizontal. What is the vertical component? (sin60° = 0.866)
items.explanation: Vertical = Fsinθ = 20 × sin60° = 20 × 0.866 = 17.3 N.

items.question: Two perpendicular forces give a resultant of magnitude 10 N. If one force is 6 N, what is the other?
items.explanation: R² = Ax² + Ay² ⇒ 10² = 6² + Ay² ⇒ Ay² = 100 − 36 = 64 ⇒ Ay = 8 N.

items.question: Why can two perpendicular 3 N forces NOT give a 6 N resultant?
items.expectedAnswer: Perpendicular vectors add by Pythagoras, giving √(3²+3²) ≈ 4.24 N, not 6 N.
items.explanation: Only parallel vectors add directly; perpendicular ones combine via Pythagoras (≈ 4.24 N).
options: Perpendicular vectors add by Pythagoras, giving √(3²+3²) ≈ 4.24 N, not 6 N.

items.question: A plane flies at 100 m·s⁻¹ east while a wind blows it 75 m·s⁻¹ north. What is its resultant ground speed?
A 50 N weight rests on a slope inclined at 30°. What is the component of the weight along the slope? (sin30° = 0.5)
items.explanation: Component along the slope = mg sinθ = 50 × sin30° = 50 × 0.5 = 25 N.

items.question: A 50 N weight rests on a slope inclined at 30°. What is the component of the weight perpendicular to the slope? (cos30° = 0.866)
items.explanation: Component perpendicular = mg cosθ = 50 × cos30° = 50 × 0.866 = 43.3 N.

items.question: When resolving a vector F at angle θ to the horizontal, which pair of components is correct?
items.explanation: Measured from the horizontal, the horizontal component is Fcosθ and the vertical is Fsinθ.
